newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Security Council, China, approve Guatemala mission.
newsitem.headline: Security Council, China, approve Guatemala mission.

text.p: With China voting in favor, the U.N. Security Council on Monday approved 155 U.N. miitary observers to peace accords in Guatemala that ended more than three decades of civil war.

The vote, the second one taken in the council in 10 days, was a unanimous 15-0. China which had vetoed a similar resolution on Jan. 10 because of Guatemala's ties to Taiwan, supported Monday's document after intensive negotiations with Guatemala and other countries.

Unclear was exactly what compromise Guatemala had made to Beijing. But diplomats said one element of an agreement between the two countries was a promise by Guatemala to refrain from co-sponsoring an annual, unsuccessful General Assembly resolution aimed at securing U.N. membership for Taiwan.
Taipei was expelled from the world body in 1971 and replaced by Beijing as the rightful representative of China.

"The Chinese side has made reasonable suggestions for the solution of this question," China's U.N. ambassador Win Huasun said in a letter to the council. "On this basis, China and Guatemala, through joint efforts have reached agreement on the relevant questions, thereby removing the obstacles to China's support for the relevant draft resolution."

Under the peace agreements, the army is to cut its numbers and about 3,000 guerrillas from the Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) are to go to assembly points, disarm and be integrated into civilian life. The process was to have begun later this week. It will be monitored by military observers who will take weeks longer to arrive.
